newsitem.title: EGYPT: U.S. firm, CIB set up offshore Egypt equities fund.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firm, CIB set up offshore Egypt equities fund.

text.p: U.S. firm Alliance Capital Management L.P. and a unit of an Egyptian bank are hoping to raise $100 million for a new joint-venture offshore mutual fund investing in Egyptian equities, a fund analyst said on Monday.
Cameron Hait, investment analyst at the fund, Nile Growth Fund Company, told Reuters the fund would close by June 3 and would be listed in Luxembourg.
ING Barings is marketing the growth-oriented fund, which will invest only in Egyptian stocks, he added.

"It's a good time for Egypt, the market looks good," Hait said. The fund will be managed by ACMCIIC Investment Management Ltd, a joint venture between Alliance and Commercial International Investment Company (CIIC), a subsidiary of private sector Commercial International Bank.

Several Egyptian banks have joined forces with foreign fund managers to set up offshore funds that invest in Egyptian securities. There are also many local funds which have holdings in stocks and government paper.
Prices on the stock exchange have been slipping in past weeks after rapid rises in the beginning of the year but brokers say the market is merely stabilising and will rise again soon.
Earlier this year, state-owned Banque Misr and the Gulf Arab Investment Company launched the first open-ended offshore fund to invest in Egyptian securities.

Last year, Concord and the state's National Bank of Egypt set up the $46 million Concord Fund, promoted by HSBC James Capel. SBC Warburg and Lazard Freres raised $74 million for the Egypt Trust and local brokerage EFG-Hermes helped raise $43 million for the Egypt Fund.
